issues.description: Deprecation message does not state behavioral contract difference between redirected() and contextlib equivalents
issues.detail: The abstract data type here is 'a context manager that temporarily replaces sys.stdout/sys.stderr.' The contract of falcon.testing.redirected accepts BOTH stdout and stderr in a single call, while contextlib.redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr each redirect only one stream. A caller migrating per the deprecation message who used `redirected(stdout=a, stderr=b)` cannot substitute a single contextlib call; they must nest two. The deprecation text should note this so callers can satisfy the new contract correctly.

issues.description: Docstring deprecation directive has typo and omits substitution guidance for dual-stream callers
issues.detail: The .. deprecated:: 4.3 directive says 'stlib' instead of 'stdlib', and like the warning text it does not tell readers how to substitute when both stdout and stderr were redirected together. Since the deprecation note is the visible contract for the migration, it should be precise and complete about the substitution pattern.

issues.description: New test does not exercise the stderr branch of the deprecated contract
issues.detail: test_deprecated_redirected verifies only the stdout path. The redirected() ADT promises redirection of stderr as well, and the deprecation must not silently change behavior for either stream before 5.0. A second assertion exercising stderr (and ideally the simultaneous-both case) would lock in the contract for the remainder of the deprecation window.

review.summary: ADT-SOUND with minor SPEC-MISSING notes. The change correctly marks redirected() as deprecated without altering its runtime contract: preconditions, postconditions, and the frame (restoration of sys.stdout/sys.stderr in the finally block) are preserved, so substitution by existing callers continues to hold through the 4.3-to-5.0 window. The chosen replacement (contextlib.redirect_stdout / redirect_stderr) is a near-equivalent abstraction, but the supertype-to-subtype mapping is not 1:1 because the stdlib functions each cover only one stream while redirected() covers both in one call; the deprecation message and docstring should state this so the advertised substitution is actually substitutable. A small typo ('stlib') and a missing stderr-path test on the deprecation are the only other nits.
